round_2_objective: FIX ROUND 1 for ticket t1: separate the arms (no fused lobe), stop the arm-chain weight leak into the face, wave in the model's frontal plane instead of sagittal, a real crouch->leap->land jump, an in-place walk loop -- per the two-probe gate findings on commit 24e24f2 (reviewer + tester + manager repro) and the manager's ruling to prefer a cleaner-bind-pose regeneration first, scripted skin-weight cleanup as a documented fallback.

pipeline.stage: 1a. image derivation - generate multiview from front reference
pipeline.reused_from: round 1 (same task_id, re-queried via get_task -- Tripo retains task results; no new credit consumed re-using it as this round's edit_multiview_image original_task_id)
pipeline.note: Tripo regenerates a consistent 4-view (front/left/back/right) turnaround from a single input image. FIX for finding #9 (provenance missing derived images): all four views of this task are committed this round (assets/kitty/derived/kitty-multiview-base-{front,left,back,right}.jpg) -- round 1 committed only the front view and left the other three neither saved nor hashed.

pipeline.stage: 1b. image derivation - LOWER arms-apart A-pose edit (regenerated this round)
pipeline.prompt_applied_to_all_four_views: Keep this exact same chubby cartoon cat completely unchanged in color, proportions, face, head tufts, ears, and curled tail -- warm yellow-orange fur, cream belly patch, big round green-and-black eyes, pink nose and tongue. Change ONLY the arm pose: move both short arms so they point outward and downward at roughly 35-40 degrees below horizontal (like a relaxed low A-pose), elbows only slightly bent, so there is a clear, unmistakable wedge of open white background between each entire arm and the torso/belly from shoulder to paw -- the paw must not touch or overlap the body silhouette. Both arms must be perfectly symmetric: identical length, identical angle, identical pose, mirrored left and right, at the same height on the torso. Do not raise the arms overhead. Do not show any extra or doubled arm shape. Only one clean arm per side, fully separated from the body outline. Legs stay in their normal standing position, feet on the ground.
pipeline.why_regenerated: Round 1's edit (task ae573a46, kept below under superseded_round_1) raised both arms overhead into a symmetric 'cheer' pose on front/back/left, but its RIGHT view broke symmetry: one arm stayed lower/pressed near the torso while the other was overhead -- a cross-view pose inconsistency that fed multiview_to_model a 3D-inconsistent target, and the reconstruction filled the gap with a second, fused arm-shaped lobe on the right flank (reviewer finding #2). It also kept the bind pose far from a neutral standing pose, which the manager's ruling flagged as the likely root cause of the arm-chain weight bleeding into the head/face (finding #1).
pipeline.result: Every one of the four re-generated views was inspected before proceeding (see assets/kitty/derived/kitty-apose-{front,back,left,right}.jpg): front/back/left/right all show exactly ONE clean arm per side, a clear gap to the torso, and (front vs back vs left vs right) no doubled or pressed lower-arm silhouette anywhere -- a materially cleaner set than round 1's. Minor residual imperfection: the raise ANGLE is not perfectly identical between the front view (~35 deg down) and the left/back/right views (~10-15 deg down, closer to horizontal); this did not reproduce any fused-limb artifact in the resulting mesh (checked by rendering the raw generated mesh from all four axis-aligned views before rigging -- see stage 2 note).

pipeline.inspection: Downloaded the raw (unrigged) mesh and rendered it from all four axis-aligned candidate views (own script, scripts/pipeline/render_preview.py's projection convention) before rigging: front/back/left/right all show exactly two arms, symmetric within ~10%, clear gap to the torso, NO extra lobe/limb on either flank. This is the check finding #2 asked for; round 1's provenance recorded only a single rendered_image inspection and missed the flank lobe.

pipeline.note: spec=tripo again this round (spec=mixamo failed animate_retarget with error 1004 in round 1's discovery -- not re-tested, no reason to expect it changed). Joints renamed Mixamo-style afterwards via scripts/pipeline/joint_rename_map.json (cosmetic, index-preserving), same as round 1.

post_rig_inspection.note: within the work order's 10% left/right symmetry bar (round 1 was 2.4x, 0.148 vs 0.362). Computed straight from the skin's inverse-bind matrices, same method the manager used to catch round 1's fused arm.
post_rig_inspection.comparison_to_round_1: round 1: 5,332/8,695 head-region vertices > 0.2 arm weight (61%). This round's regenerated, closer-to-neutral bind pose alone cut that to 768/5,757 (13%) before any scripted cleanup -- consistent with the manager's ruling that a cleaner-bind-pose regeneration is the preferred fix, with scripted cleanup only needed for the remainder.

pipeline.stage: 4b. skin-weight cleanup (scripted, documented fallback per the manager's ruling)
pipeline.why: Regeneration alone (stage 1b/2/4 above) removed the fused-arm lobe entirely and cut head/neck arm-weight leakage from 61% to 13% of head/neck-dominant vertices, but did not reach zero. Per the manager's ruling, a documented scripted cleanup is an acceptable fallback for the remainder: this script zeroes arm-chain (shoulder/upper-arm/forearm/hand, both twist bones) weight on any vertex NOT dominated by that arm chain -- i.e. off every Head/Neck/torso/leg/tail vertex and off the OTHER (non-dominant) arm -- and renormalizes. It is a pure per-vertex weight edit: no geometry, joint hierarchy, or bind pose is touched.
pipeline.result: 0/5,757 Head-or-Neck-dominant vertices now carry any arm-chain weight (was 768); 0 cross-contamination between the left and right arm chains. 5,184/13,286 total vertices (39%) had some weight adjusted, all of it weight that would otherwise have dragged a non-arm vertex when only one arm animates.

pipeline.note: re-retargeted against this round's new rig (round 1's idle clip was against the old, fused-arm rig and can't be reused). Verified: every channel loops (first sample == last sample) within tolerance already, no fix needed.

pipeline.stage: 5b. animation - jump (AUTHORED this round; preset retarget fetched, diagnosed, and discarded)
pipeline.preset_diagnosis: Sampled the retargeted preset with scripts/pipeline/gltf_anim.py: Hips oscillates 0.174-0.278 (5 repeating bounces over the clip's 2.233s), the single best individual bounce clears only ~9.4% of model height measured from the CLIP's own start frame (below the work order's >=10%h bar for accepting a preset sub-range) -- and qualitatively it reads as a bounce loop, not the spec's 'anticipation crouch -> leap -> land'. Per the work order ('use a preset sub-range if one hop meets that, otherwise author it on the rig'), this was authored instead.

authored_replacement.mechanics: Hips translates along the rig's own verified world-up axis (crouch dip -> leap rise -> land); Thigh/Calf rotate about the rig's verified world-Z hinge axis for a small anticipation/landing knee bend (kept deliberately shallow -- this character's stubby legs self-intersect the belly mesh at a more 'realistic' bend angle, checked visually via render_preview.py before reducing it). Every other joint (arms, spine, head) pinned to the idle clip's frame-0 pose; Root translation stays at 0 throughout (in place).

pipeline.stage: 5c. animation - walk (preset retargeted, then scripted in-place fix)
pipeline.diagnosis: Sampled every channel's first vs. last keyframe: only Hips.translation differs (56.9% of model height net drift along the model's forward axis) -- Root itself never moves, and every rotation channel plus the other two translation axes already loop perfectly.

fix.method: Linearly detrend the Hips local-translation axes with first!=last (identified automatically, not hard-coded) so each equals its own first sample exactly at the clip's end, leaving the cyclic in-between shape (gait sway/bob) untouched.
fix.result: Hips world-space translation range now: X 1.55%h, Y (vertical bob) 0.80%h, Z (lateral sway, in-cycle only) 7.0%h; first-frame == last-frame on every channel within tolerance (V5).

pipeline.stage: 5d. animation - wave (authored, no Tripo preset exists) -- REWRITTEN this round for the frontal-plane fix
pipeline.note: Tripo's preset library has no 'wave' motion (unchanged from round 1). Round 1's script rotated the shoulder/forearm about the model's world Z axis, sweeping the arm through the SAGITTAL (forward/back) plane -- reviewer finding #3. This round's facing axis was RE-VERIFIED for the regenerated mesh (not assumed carried over): rendering the raw model from four axis-aligned candidate cameras shows the face square-on only from world +X, so the frontal plane (up x left-right) is Y-Z, and the fix is to rotate about world X instead. Per-side sign (which way is 'outward + up' for each arm) was verified numerically via forward kinematics on the neutral pose before picking defaults, not assumed symmetric.

All four clips share one skeleton+skin (idle/jump/walk trace back to rig task ee15e4b9; wave and the authored jump are keyframed directly on that same rig's base, post skin-cleanup). Channels copied by joint NAME (not raw index) from each source clip onto the CLEANED base rigged model (stage 4b's output), per the work order.

scripts_used.render_preview_textured.py: NEW this round: a z-buffered, numpy-vectorized software rasterizer that samples the model's own PBR base-color texture via UV coordinates (round 1's render_preview.py was flat-shaded/untextured -- advisory finding #16).
